answer.evidence: The main body is a raised platform. Rows 15-31 are a wide plank floor with a back rail, and rows 12-14 show the rail posts. The floor ends in a light front-edge line at row 32 (#d59147), followed by darker shadow in rows 33-35. Below that, a dark brown front face runs from row 33 to row 41, with the ladder hanging over it down to row 46. The side rails are narrow vertical strips at the silhouette edges, not receding side faces. The ladder is a thin vertical element and does not need a top.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a wooden platform with a rail and ladder, drawn with a dark brown outline that leans toward the wood. The measured near-neutral share of dark edge pixels is 0%, so this is not a black sticker line. It shows 12 visible tones per 16x16 tile and 0% near-flat coverage. That is above the hedge (9) and below the stall (17) and well (20), and the references have far more raw colours overall (38-40 against 18). The wood ramp has about 5 steps, covering the light top deck, plank faces, shadowed rail and ladder, which is slightly under the 6 steps of the richer references. Plank seams and grain keep the front face and deck from being flat fills. It would sit acceptably beside the references, though it is a little simpler than the stall and well.

answer.evidence: The deck is a wide plank floor over rows 15-31 with scattered nail pixels, which is a clear horizontal surface seen from above. It ends in a light orange front-edge line at row 32, and the dark front face of the base sits below it in rows 33-41. The back rail (rows 9-11) and the posts (rows 12-14) stand on the deck and are thin structural railing, not a main volume. The ladder is a thin element in front, with two rails and rungs over rows 30-46. The silhouette is 30 px wide through rows 15-40, and no receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a wooden platform with a rail and ladder, and it matches the prop references in kind and scale. It has 12 visible tones per 16x16 tile, which is above the hedge (9) and below the stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is a tinted dark brown beside the wood, not a sticker-style black line. The planks, posts and ladder rungs are separated by value, and the wood carries about 4 lightness steps with plank grain. That is slightly fewer than the roughly 5 on the stall and well wood. The total of 18 distinct colours is modest, but it is comparable to the hedge reference (11 colours), and the facts show no flatness or outline problem. A careful artist would accept it next to the references, though it is a little simpler than the stall and the well.

answer.evidence: The main body is a raised platform. Rows 15-31 are a wide plank deck with horizontal board bands, ending in a light orange front-edge line at row 32 (#d59147). Darker shadow and the front face follow in rows 33-41, so the front face is about 9 rows. A railing runs along the back (rows 9-14) and down the sides. The ladder in rows 30-47 is a thin structural element placed against the front face. No isometric side face is drawn. The deck is a clear horizontal surface above a front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a wooden platform with a railing and a ladder. It has 12 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat coverage and 0% neutral dark edges, so the outlines carry a brown tint. That is comparable to the hedge (9) and below the stall (17) and well (20). The wood shows plank lines and a few light/dark steps, about 4 per material, against the 5-6 steps in the references. The railing and ladder are drawn cleanly, but the large front face and deck look somewhat smooth and have less grain, knots and speckle than the stall or well. There are no flat 5x5 fills. It would sit beside the references acceptably, but it looks a little thinner in texture and shading. Because the guidance says to fail when in doubt, this is borderline.
